title: AWQ: Activation-aware Weight Quantization for LLM Compression and Acceleration
technique: activation-aware per-channel scaling to protect ~1% salient weights in 4-bit weight-only quantization; TinyChat inference framework with fused dequant kernels

optimized_metrics.evidence: We focus on the second setting in this work since it not only reduces the hardware barrier (requiring a smaller memory size) but also speeds up the token generation (remedies memory-bound workload).
while post-training quantization (PTQ) suffers from large accuracy degradation under a low-bit setting.

headline_claim.text: TinyChat offers more than 3x speedup over the Huggingface FP16 implementation on both desktop and mobile GPUs. It also democratizes the deployment of the 70B Llama-2 model on mobile GPUs.

metric_definitions.definition_quote: We perform batch size = 1 inference for all LLMs using a fixed prompt length of 4 tokens. We generate 200 tokens for each inference run and calculate the median latency as the final result.
metric_definitions.notes: Speed reported as tokens/s at batch 1 (e.g. Llama-2-7B 52 -> 62 tokens/s from FP16 kernel fusion, then 3.1x more from quantized kernels); speedup baseline is Huggingface FP16.

load_regime: batch=1, 4-token prompt, 200 generated tokens, median over runs
tradeoff_acknowledged: W8A8 methods unsuitable for on-device generation stage (arithmetic intensity ~1; memory-bound), so weight-only 4-bit chosen; context stage is compute-bound and 10 ms for 200 tokens vs 310 ms to generate 20 tokens
hardware: RTX 4090, RTX 4070 laptop, Jetson Orin, Raspberry Pi 4B, Apple M1
models: Llama/Llama-2, OPT, MPT, Falcon, Vicuna, OpenFlamingo, VILA
workloads: WikiText perplexity, MMLU, coding/math benchmarks, VLM benchmarks
extractor_notes: Edge/on-device, batch 1; no serving, no percentiles. Latency profile shows generation stage dominates (310 ms for 20 tokens vs 10 ms for 200-token prompt) which motivates weight-only quantization.
